jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100\* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.*

**An overview of this role**
----------------------------

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.

We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
* Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
* Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
* Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
* Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) …

jobs.description:
Overview 
Find the problem. Decide what to build. Ship it to production and prove it worked.
 Reporting to the CTO.
 Company Details 
Periskope helps businesses run customer conversations and operations on WhatsApp. Chats, groups, ticketing and automation live in one workspace, used by teams around the world.
 $2.5M+ ARR
 ~12 People
 Profitable · Global customers
 Seed · Saison Capital and Alliance
 Requirements
 2–5 years: In engineering, product, a founder's office, or your own startup.
 Product intuition: You can look at a screen and say what is wrong with it, and why.
 Proof you build: Something real you made with AI tools. A product, an internal tool, an automation people still use.
 Hustle: You unblock yourself. You do not wait for a spec, a designer or permission.
 Appetite for depth: You do not need to know production systems today. You need to want to own them.
 Clear communication: You explain decisions, flag uncertainty early, and move work forward in a remote team.
 Responsibilities
 Customer problems: Talk to users every week. Turn what you hear into a clear call on what to build next.
 Concept to production: Scope it, build it with agents, deploy it, and iterate on real usage.
 A product surface: Own a part of Periskope end to end, and the metric it moves.
 What ships: Challenge agent output, test assumptions, and stay accountable for the code and the result.
 Production reliability: When something breaks, find out why and fix it. Learn the data models, APIs and WhatsApp infrastructure underneath.
 Job Details
 Remote for candidates based in India.
 Interview Process 
Share your profile and one thing you took from idea to shipped: the problem, what you built, how you used agents, and what changed. Shortlisted candidates move through three steps.
 Conversation · Async on WhatsApp 
Talk through your work and product decisions with Bharat (CTO).
 Build together · 90 minutes 
Take a real Periskope problem from brief to working build, live with Bharat.
 Final conversation · 20 minutes 
Discuss the role and mutual fit with Swapnika (CEO).
 Why This Role Exists 
For years, building software needed two people. A PM decided what to build. An engineer wrote the code. Most of the time went into the handoff between them.
 That split no longer makes sense. AI agents now write most of our code. Typing code stopped being the bottleneck. Judgment took its place: knowing which problem matters, what the smallest useful fix is, and whether it holds up in production.
 A Product Engineer is one person doing the whole loop. You talk to the customer, make the call, direct the agents, ship the change and watch what happens next.
 How the Work Flows
 Listen: Sales calls, support chats, churn reasons, usage data.
 Decide: Pick the problem that matters. Cut it to the smallest useful fix.
 Build: Direct agents. Review every diff. Test what they assume.
 Ship: Release to real customers, behind a flag if it is risky.
 Measure: Check usage and tickets. Keep it, fix it or kill it.
 Then back to listening. A good loop takes days, not quarters.
 Who This Is For 
You do not need an engineering title. You need taste, speed, and a real wish to build things that run in production.
 Engineers: Who care more about the customer than the stack.
 Product managers: Who are tired of writing specs for someone else to build.
 Founder's office operators: Who already do a bit of everything and want to ship software too.
 Ex-founders: Who want to build product again, …
